title: Type-B double-Fock Wick formula with crossing and negative-pair weights for real simple tensors
author: Marek Bozejko; Wiktor Ejsmont
source_title: The Double Fock Space of Type B
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a weighted correspondence between double creation/annihilation histories and reflection-symmetric pair-and-singleton partitions. In the negative and positive annihilation cases it tracks crossings and covered singletons separately, obtaining the different powers of q and the negative-pair power of alpha. A bijective induction then removes the singletons under vacuum expectation to establish the full joint moment formula, rather than calculating a single Gaussian marginal.
source_version: Official SIGMA 19 (2023) article 040, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2023.040; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read the complete Theorem4.6 proof and the explicit positive/negative annihilation formulas (3.1)–(3.2). The double Fock construction is on the complexification of a separable real Hilbert space, alpha,q in (-1,1), and selected arguments are real simple tensors. The underlying Coxeter positivity and parabolic decomposition are prior established results. The adjoint identification Proposition3.6 is the elementary construction obtained from that decomposition; its explicit resulting operator formula is present and used by the proof. The omitted norm estimates in Theorem3.9 are not needed for this algebraic vacuum-moment identity and are not claimed. All partition statistics, both inductive cases and the exhaustive final pairing sum are retained.
